All five current concentration blocks are preserved as mutually exclusive alternates to the no-concentration upper-level CS requirement; they are not aggregated into the base path.
Advanced Computer Science has its own 7-8 credit B.S. science list plus a Major Field Test and C-or-better CS-course rule; these variant-only gates do not apply to the base path.

The published 55-88 major-credit banner and 41-74 open-credit range do not reconcile with the named mutually exclusive path arithmetic and 120-credit total; preserve the explicit rows and flag the conflict rather than treating either range as an additive requirement.

REAL is an integrated 48-hour framework that can be fulfilled by major, minor, and degree work. The program separately requires at least 30 GE-designated credits; do not add 48 gross credits on top of the major.
Exclude the separate Virginia Tech accelerated M.Eng. pathway from the standard 120-credit B.S. model.

groups.title: Advanced Artificial Intelligence Concentration
groups.note: The Advanced Computer Science concentration prepares students for a variety of technology careers or graduate study by building a broad foundation in the computer science core. The Advanced Database, Advanced Networks, Advanced Artifical Intelligence and Advanced Software Engineering concentrations provide graduates with a breadth of technical experience and a depth of knowledge in a particular application area. This major fulfills the R and L areas of the REAL Curriculum. Students fulfill the R area through classes though the skills and knowledge gained in a calculus class, programming classes and a discrete math course. Students fulfill the L area through classes developing and reflecting on their professional skills, experience and abilities in a number of classes teaching skills in area such as networks, web site development, databases and software development. Students need majors and/or minors to fulfill the E and A areas to complete the REAL Curriculum requirements.
source_text: Students seeking the Bachelor of Science in Computer Science must complete the University’s REAL Curriculum Requirements, the Degree Core Requirements, the Bachelor of Science Requirements, and either four 3XX or 4XX CS courses (except CS 307, 398, 493, 498, 352, 371, 445,455,465,475) or complete the courses for one of concentrations. Students may also use any 500 or 600-level CS course approved by the School Director to fulfill any of the four classes listed earlier. Students can choose at least one of the five concentrations within the major in addition to the major itself: Advanced Computer Science, Advanced Databases, Advanced Networks, Advanced Artifical Intelligence, and Advanced Software Engineering.
